nodes.title: GET /api/keys has no organisation arm: an ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN lists another organisation's keys in the same tenant
nodes.description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **has no organisation arm.** An `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A lists organisation B's API keys when B is in the same tenant, using B's exact id. The mint and the revoke are both organisation-bounded for these roles; the list is the only one of the three routes that is not. **Measured** at develop `7c6b3d88`, details below. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's ruling while building KS-1553 PR 1, which does **not** add the bound.

**What is exposed:** each key's **id, name, prefix, scopes and connector id**, plus `lastUsedAt`, `usageCount`, `isActive` and `createdAt`. **Not key material:** the list never returns the key or its hash.

**Not reached by Kam's ADMIN ruling.** That ruling (KS-1570) concerns the tenant-level `ADMIN` role on the mint. The roles here are `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, which are organisation-bounded on the mint (KS-1533) and on the revoke (KS-764).

## The code

At develop `7c6b3d88`, `services/security/src/index.ts:1318-1366`:

* The handler filters `k.organizationId === organizationId`, where `organizationId` is the raw query value, and then `callerIsPlatform || k.tenantId === caller.tenantId`. That second filter is KS-742's tenant bound.
* Nothing in the handler reads `caller.organizationId` or calls `isOrgBoundedRole`.
* The mint, by contrast, calls `decideTenantAccess(user, tenantId, { targetOrganizationId })` (`index.ts:1173`). That engages the organisation arm for `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES = {ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN}` (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`).
* The revoke is bounded by `decideKeyRevoke` (KS-764).

## Measured

A throwaway in-process probe, using the same harness as `ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts` (memory-backed; the list reads only `memApiKeys`). Organisation ids contain hex letters, so the upper-case form is not identical to the original.

| caller | lists | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| platform (`super_admin`) | mints for A1 and A2 | 201, 201 |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A1 | 200, 1 key |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of A1** | **A2, exact id** | **200, 1 key (the gap)** |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A2, upper-case | 200, 0 keys (only because the compare is raw; see below) |
| CONTROL: `ISSUER_ADMIN` of a tenant-B org | A2 | 200, 0 keys (the tenant filter is real) |
| CONTROL: platform | A2 | 200, 1 key |

**After KS-1553 PR 1** the list normalises the query, so the upper-case form of A2 also lists A2's key. That reveals nothing the exact id does not already reveal. PR 1 pins both as cells labelled MEASURED GAP that name this ticket, so adding a bound later is a visible edit.

## Dedupe

I scanned all 1,560 issues, archived ones included, with their comments, for list / another-organisation / organisation-arm wording. The positive control (KS-1533 matching "organisation arm") fired, and a bogus-symbol control returned 0. Nothing covers the list. KS-742 bounded the list by **tenant** only.

## Not decided here

The shape of the bound: refuse, or filter as KS-742 and `GET /api/audit` do. Also how it treats the org-less bounded accounts KS-779 recorded as intentional.
